perf.summary: Narrowing long->int copy with explicit (int) cast is already Burst-vectorizable; only note is to confirm it is the intended truncation, not saturation.
perf.currentCost: Per-element 64->32-bit truncating store; Burst can vectorize the narrowing pack, so cost is near memory-bandwidth bound already.
perf.proposedChange: No code change needed for correctness/perf. If callers ever pass values outside int range expecting clamping, that is NOT what this does (it truncates the low 32 bits). Document the truncation contract in a comment so the unchecked Run convention is explicit.
perf.rationale: The loop is already optimal for Burst (contiguous load, narrow, store; SIMD pack). There is no asymptotic or constant-factor win to extract; flagging it would be cargo-cult.
perf.risk: None for behavior. Truncation (int)long differs from clamping only for out-of-range inputs, which the unchecked Run contract already assumes valid; no change proposed.
